question: What will be US retail sales excluding food services, not seasonally adjusted (Census Bureau) for July 2026, as first published?

research:
I used only data published on or before 2026-08-04. I found and ignored some pages dated after the cutoff.

## 1. Resolution source
- The question resolves on FRED series RSXFSN (Census Advance Retail Sales: Retail Trade, not seasonally adjusted, millions of dollars). The first published July 2026 value comes with the Census advance release on about 2026-08-14.
- 2026-08-01 (ALFRED vintage): the latest value is June 2026 = **672,368**. This matches the baseline you supplied. Earlier 2026 values: Jan 582,287; Feb 564,663; Mar 657,586; Apr 654,070; May 685,407. [ALFRED vintage csv](https://alfred.stlouisfed.org/graph/alfredgraph.csv?id=RSXFSN&vintage_date=2026-08-01&cosd=2019-01-01)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet. The July advance report is not out before forecasts close.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- Mid-July 2026: an aggregator put AAA regular gasoline at about $3.99 a gallon, with the EIA weekly average at $3.855 on Jul 13. Prices were falling from a 2026 peak of about $4.56 on May 21, but are well above July 2025 levels (about $3.15, my recollection, not checked). That points to a large year-over-year gain at gas stations. [walnutinvest](https://walnutinvest.com/stats/gas-price-statistics), [Washington Examiner](https://www.washingtonexaminer.com/?p=4616127)
- 2026-07-16: June advance report. Retail and food services $768.6B seasonally adjusted, +0.2% m/m, +6.7% y/y. April-June was +6.4% y/y. Gas station receipts fell 5.3% as pump prices dropped after the US-Iran memorandum of understanding (MoU). Ex-gas sales rose 0.7% (+5.7% y/y), the control group rose 0.5%, and May was revised up to +1.0%. [trade.gov.tr](https://trade.gov.tr/news/u-s-retail-sales-up-6-7-yoy-in-june-2026), [Haver](https://www.haver.com/articles/u-s-retail-sales-in-june-slowed-by-drop-in-gasoline-sales), [investinglive](https://investinglive.com/news/us-june-retail-sales-vs-0-2-expected)

## 4. Base rates and seasonality
These figures are from the 2026-08-01 vintage.

**July/June ratio and value implied for July 2026 (applied to June's 672,368):**

| Year | June | July | Jul/Jun | Implied Jul 2026 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2019 | 440,356 | 453,537 | 1.030 | ~692,500 |
| 2021 | 547,334 | 542,000 | 0.990 | ~665,800 |
| 2022 | 594,419 | 584,625 | 0.984 | ~661,300 |
| 2023 | 597,476 | 591,150 | 0.989 | ~665,300 |
| 2024 | 592,999 | 618,432 | 1.043 | ~701,200 |
| 2025 | 616,031 | 644,493 | 1.046 | ~703,400 |

- The ratio has swung widely (0.98 to 1.05). The swing probably reflects day-of-week composition and when Prime Day falls. In 2024 and 2025, June was weak relative to May (-6.1% and -4.8%).
- **Caution:** in 2026, June fell only 1.9% from May (685,407 to 672,368). This year's June is unusually strong relative to May, so a straight ratio may overstate July.

**Year-over-year approach (July 2025 = 644,493):**
- Not-seasonally-adjusted y/y in 2026: Jan +2.8%, Feb +3.8%, Mar +5.2%, Apr +4.9%, May +5.9%, Jun +9.1%.
- June is boosted by the calendar. June 2026 had 22 weekdays and 4 Sundays, against 21 weekdays and 5 Sundays in June 2025.
- Implied July 2026 values: +4% gives ~670,300; +5% gives ~676,700; +6% gives ~683,200; +7% gives ~689,600.

**Calendar:**
- July 2026 starts on a Wednesday and has five Wednesdays, Thursdays and Fridays.
- July 2025 started on a Tuesday and had five Tuesdays, Wednesdays and Thursdays. This year swaps one Tuesday for a Friday, a small plus.
- Both Julys have 4 Saturdays and 4 Sundays.

**Your statistical baseline:** median about 677,000, p25 to p75 about 652,000 to 705,000. That is broader than the year-over-year approach suggests.

## 5. Other forecasts
- Manifold has markets on the July 2026 seasonally adjusted headline, but I could not get pre-cutoff prices. [Manifold](https://manifold.markets/CalibratedGhosts/will-july-2026-us-advance-retail-sa)
- I found no dated pre-cutoff consensus for July's headline m/m change. The sources I found that list a consensus are dated after the cutoff, so I did not use them.
- Coresight published a "July 2026 US Retail Sales Outlook" projecting about 5% growth for the rest of summer. I could not confirm its publication date or whether it measures the same thing. [Coresight](https://coresight.com/research/july-2026-us-retail-sales-outlook-promotional-activity-and-early-back-to-school-shopping-drive-sales-growth/)
- I found no Kalshi or Polymarket market on the not-seasonally-adjusted level.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- About 2026-08-14 at 8:30 ET: the Census July advance report, which sets the resolution value. June may also be revised, but that does not affect resolution.
- Before then, the main inputs are July auto sales (released in early August), July CPI gasoline prices (out before retail sales), and Prime Day timing and card-spending trackers.
- This is not a weather-driven series.
